an3.51:1.1: Then two brahmins who were old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, come to the last stage, a hundred and twenty years of age, approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
an3.51:1.2: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, they sat down to one side and said to the Blessed One:
an3.51:1.3: “We are brahmins, Master Gotama, old, aged … a hundred and twenty years of age.
an3.51:1.4: But we have not done anything good and wholesome, nor have we made a shelter for ourselves.
an3.51:1.5: Let Master Gotama exhort us and instruct us in a way that will lead to our welfare and happiness for a long time!”
an3.51:2.1: “Truly, brahmins, you are old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, come to the last stage, a hundred and twenty years of age,
an3.51:2.2: but you have not done anything good and wholesome, nor have you made a shelter for yourselves.
an3.51:2.3: Indeed, this world is swept away by old age, illness, and death.
an3.51:2.4: But though the world is swept away by old age, illness, and death, when one has departed, bodily, verbal, and mental self-control will provide a shelter, a harbor, an island, a refuge, and a support.”
an3.51:3.1: Life is swept along, short is the life span,
an3.51:3.2: no shelters exist for one who has grown old.
an3.51:3.3: Seeing clearly this peril in death,
an3.51:3.4: one should do deeds of merit that bring happiness.
an3.51:4.2: self-control over body, speech, and mind,
an3.51:4.4: and the deeds of merit one did while living,
